name: Harold Crawford
life: “I still remember being asked for a medical opinion at my own beach picnic.” Monday often includes a stop at Juniper Street, where Harold knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I am her doctor and emphatically don't get to decide how she spends an ordinary evening.
appearance: Harold is easy to recognize by a dark undercut with a longer wave on top and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a rust-colored canvas coat with a replacement button a shade darker than the others, Harold looks toward the door whenever a name is called when listening.
personality: Harold has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Harold's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To respect the swimmer's control over the evening.
family: Gareth Jiang is Harold’s cousin raised in the same household. Harold sets the time to leave. Gareth picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The understudy sings*, Gareth says, “I read lips in rehearsals. I offered to teach both singers without asking either for a diagnosis.”
connections: Milo Neal. The swimmer's sibling and physician both give up the temptation to decide for someone else.
